articles.title: The Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group Announces New Hours for Fall
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in November.
body: The Marsh Landing Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Julia Garrity, who has lived in Marsh Landing for 35 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.
The plan calls for second recycling drop-off along Dayton Road, with work expected to start in November. The group has raised $3,400 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Playground Upgrade
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in October.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 12 weeks once it begins. The Cedar Hollow Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The plan calls for playground upgrade along Coal Drive, with work expected to start in October. The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Bernadette Esposito, who has lived in Cedar Hollow for 12 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Letter: the Canal Park Food Pantry Did a Good Job This Fall
body: To the editor: I have lived on Juniper Lane for 38 years, and I want to say what a difference the Canal Park Food Pantry has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the September meeting. Please keep the summer concert series in the budget. Many of us on Juniper Lane use it every week.
Cyrus Renner, Eastgate

articles.title: Council Approves $3,400 for Crane Terrace Repairs
articles.deck: The vote came after 32 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Councilmember Hal Thibodeaux asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $3,400.
Residents of Stonebridge said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Council Splits 4–3 on Second Recycling Drop-off
articles.deck: The vote came after 11 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 11 weeks once it starts in April.
Residents of Cedar Hollow said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Councilmember Sergio Farrow asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $1,200.

articles.title: Lower Millrace Volunteers Host Spring Drive
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 16 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: Simone Sandoval, who has lived on Pine Drive for 16 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings.
The effort began in January when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about park bench program.

articles.title: Albert McIver, 91, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Albert McIver for the many years of service to Cedar Hollow.
body: Albert McIver died in October at home on Mulberry Road, at the age of 91. Born in Cedar Hollow in the years after the war, Albert McIver spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Lower Millrace Improvement Group in his or her name.

articles.title: Council Splits 4–3 on Streetlight Upgrade
articles.deck: The vote came after 8 residents spoke at Friday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Councilmember Hannah Vance asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $3,400. Residents of Kettle Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 8 weeks once it starts in February.

articles.title: Upper Commons Garden Club Adds Streetlight Upgrade
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 15 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: The effort began in May when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about streetlight upgrade.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings.

Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Foundry Row fire house on Monday at 7 p.m. Several residents on Harbor Court said they had been waiting since 1993 for something like this.

articles.title: The Cedar Hollow Garden Club Opens Sidewalk Ramp on Orion Drive
articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row met on Friday to talk over the plan.
body: The Foundry Row Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Foundry Row fire house on Friday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Sidewalk Ramp Near Mill Hill
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Pearl Lane disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Mill Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 10 weeks once it starts in September. Councilmember Helena Demetriou asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $1,200.

articles.title: Letters: Birch Terrace Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I have lived on Birch Terrace for 39 years, and I want to say what a difference St. Brendan’s Parish has made.
Please keep the accessible ramp in the budget. Many of us on Birch Terrace use it every week.
Xavier Baptiste, Kettle Hill

articles.title: Letters: Carver Drive Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I have lived on Carver Drive for 18 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group has made.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. Please keep the bus shelter in the budget. Many of us on Carver Drive use it every week.
Quentin Beaudry, Hickory Ridge

articles.title: Patrice Salazar, 80, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Patrice Salazar for the many years of service to Marsh Landing.
body: Patrice Salazar died in October at home on Meadow Court, at the age of 80. Born in Marsh Landing in the years after the war, Patrice Salazar spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center in his or her name.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Marsh Landing.

articles.title: The Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. Opens Footpath Repair on Copper Place
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 38 people and say footpath repair is the main draw.
body: Eleanor Esposito, who has lived on Copper Place for 38 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Tuesday mornings. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Cedar Hollow Pavilion on Tuesday at 7 p.m.

body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Bellwood Chapel on Thursday at 7 p.m. Bernadette Brennan, who has lived on Yardley Avenue for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
